report.summary: Chunk 4 of slice.py: neighborhood construction with egress gating and symbol-path scope boundary reassertion.

handoff.purpose: Neighborhood edge filtering, document link separation, egress gating, and symbol-path scope boundary reassertion.

symbols.name: _rule_for
symbols.note: Cached rule lookup via slice_egress_rule; accesses filesystem through _read.

symbols.name: _emit_ok
symbols.note: Returns boolean; populates withheld_map if rule exists.

claims.why: Both statements are present and executed in order.

claims.text: dep_rels and caller_rels are built by iterating over edges.get(rel,()) and rev_edges.get(rel,()) respectively, skipping self-loops and filtering on r in modules.
claims.why: The loops and conditions match the claim.

claims.text: shell_stops counts edges whose target is not in modules.
claims.why: Incremented when r not in modules (or src not in modules) and r != rel.

claims.text: doc_edges and doc_rev are kept separate from dep_rels/caller_rels because a link is not an import, and to avoid manufacturing call edges out of prose.
claims.why: The comment explicitly states the two reasons; code builds separate sets documents_out and documented_by.

claims.text: Both maps are absent from an index built without documents, so this is inert by construction on the default path.
claims.why: The chunk does not show the index building logic; the claim refers to behaviour outside this chunk.

claims.text: The egress gate is applied at the emission point of every file whose text would enter slice_text, gating each emitted unit's module.
claims.why: The chunk defines the gate functions but does not show the emission code that uses them.

claims.text: Floor (secret-only) applies in every lane; the default-deny allow-list only in an untrusted lane.
claims.why: The chunk does not define lane or policy; the claim refers to external configuration.

claims.text: Per file, so the deny_content first-match-break cannot poison a whole slice and every hit is attributable to one path.
claims.why: The chunk does not show the deny_content logic; the claim refers to behaviour outside this chunk.

claims.text: Reported, never silent: withheld -> a sorted block + an inline breadcrumb.
claims.why: The chunk does not show emission or reporting logic.

claims.text: If symbol and focus_unit is not None and not is_doc, then symbol-level resolution is performed using graph.callees and graph.callers.
claims.why: The conditional and the calls match the claim.

claims.text: graph.callees and graph.callers are called with resolver from resolution_context(root, key=idx.get("scope_key")).
The scope boundary is re-asserted on the symbol path because the resolver reads defs_by_file directly and can return shell units.
claims.why: The chunk does not contain the actual re-assertion logic (the comment describes it but the code is not shown).

claims.text: Rejections are counted into the same shell_boundary_stops the module path reports.
claims.why: The chunk does not show where shell_boundary_stops is defined or incremented in this path.

The scope boundary re-assertion is described in detail but the actual filtering logic is not present in this chunk.
